indikativ.title: Indikativ
indikativ.summary: The mood of facts: what happens, happened or will happen.
body: The indicative presents something as real. It is the normal mood of German.

head: Tense
Example
Expresses
rows: Now, habits, truths, and very often the future
The past in writing and narrative
Intentions, predictions, guesses about the present
Completed by a future moment, guesses about the past

body.h: Fewer past tenses than Italian or Spanish

body: German makes no distinction like *imperfetto* against *passato remoto*. Perfekt and Präteritum differ mainly in style, not in meaning: speech prefers the first, writing the second.

In a main clause the conjugated verb is in second position, and any participle or infinitive goes to the end: *Ich {pp:habe} gestern lange {pp:gearbeitet}.* In a subordinate clause the conjugated verb goes last: *..., weil ich lange {pp:gearbeitet habe}.*

praesens.title: Präsens
praesens.summary: Now, habits, general truths, and very often the future.
body: Remove *-en* and add the endings. If the stem ends in *-t* or *-d*, or in certain consonant groups, an *e* is inserted to help pronunciation.
The vowel change happens only in *du* and *er / sie / es*, and only in strong verbs: *laufen: läufst; lesen: liest; nehmen: nimmst; geben: gibst*.
The prefix goes to the end of the clause: *aufstehen: Ich {ip:stehe} um sieben {ip:auf}.*

ul: Now: *Ich {ip:lese} gerade die Zeitung.*
Habits: *Montags {ip:gehe} ich ins Fitnessstudio.*
General truths: *Wasser {ip:kocht} bei hundert Grad.*
The future, with a time word. This is the normal way to talk about it: *Morgen {ip:fahre} ich nach Berlin.*
An action that still continues, with *seit*: *Ich {ip:lerne} seit zwei Jahren Deutsch.*

perfekt.title: Perfekt
perfekt.summary: The past tense of everyday speech.
body: Use the present of *haben* or *sein*, and put the Partizip II at the end of the clause.

ul: Most verbs take *haben*, including all with a direct object and all reflexive verbs.
*Sein* goes with verbs of movement from one place to another and changes of state: *gehen, fahren, kommen, aufstehen, einschlafen, sterben, werden*.
*Sein* also goes with *sein, bleiben* and *passieren*.

head: Type
Pattern
Examples
rows: sprechen: gesprochen; finden: gefunden; fahren: gefahren
denken: gedacht; bringen: gebracht; kennen: gekannt

ul: Talking about the past in conversation: *Gestern {pp:habe} ich einen Film {pp:gesehen}.*
Past events that matter now: *Ich {pp:habe} meine Schlüssel {pp:verloren}.*
It also translates the *passato remoto* of spoken narrative: anything told aloud usually takes Perfekt.

plusquamperfekt.title: Plusquamperfekt
body: Use the Präteritum of *haben* or *sein* and the Partizip II. The choice of auxiliary is the same as in the Perfekt.

ul: An action completed before another past event: *Als ich {pr:ankam}, {tp:war} der Zug schon {tp:abgefahren}.*
After *nachdem*: *Nachdem ich {tp:gegessen hatte}, {pr:ging} ich spazieren.*
The cause of a past situation: *Ich {pr:war} müde, weil ich viel {tp:gearbeitet hatte}.*

praeteritum.title: Präteritum
praeteritum.summary: The past tense of writing and storytelling.
body: Weak verbs add *-te* plus the ending. Strong verbs change their vowel and add no ending in *ich* and *er / sie / es*.
Mixed verbs have a new vowel and the weak ending: *denken: dachte; bringen: brachte; wissen: wusste; kennen: kannte.*

body.h: The verbs that use it in speech

ul: Novels, news and written accounts: *Der König {pr:lebte} in einem großen Schloss.*
*Sein*, *haben* and modal verbs, even in speech: *Ich {pr:war} krank und {pr:konnte} nicht kommen.*
It covers both the *imperfetto* and the *passato remoto*: *Es {pr:regnete}* is a description, and *Er {pr:öffnete} die Tür* is an event.

futur_1.title: Futur I
futur_1.summary: Intentions, promises, predictions and guesses about the present.
body: Use the present of *werden* and put the infinitive at the end of the clause.

ul: Promises and firm intentions: *Ich {fs:werde} dir {fs:helfen}.*
Predictions: *Es {fs:wird} morgen {fs:regnen}.*
A guess about the present, often with *wohl*: *Er {fs:wird} wohl zu Hause {fs:sein}.*

body: When the time is clear, German usually prefers the Präsens: *Morgen {ip:rufe} ich dich {ip:an}.*

futur_2.title: Futur II
futur_2.summary: What will already have happened, and guesses about the past.
body: Use the present of *werden*, then the Partizip II and *haben* or *sein* at the end.

ul: An action finished by a future moment: *Bis morgen {fa:werde} ich es {fa:geschafft haben}.*
A guess about the past, often with *wohl*: *Er {fa:wird} den Zug wohl {fa:verpasst haben}.*

body: In everyday speech, the Perfekt often replaces it for future completion: *Bis morgen {pp:habe} ich es {pp:geschafft}.*

konjunktiv_2.title: Konjunktiv II
konjunktiv_2.summary: The mood of the unreal: what would be, politeness, wishes and advice.
body: It does the work of the Italian *condizionale* and much of the *congiuntivo imperfetto* and *trapassato*. The names Gegenwart and Vergangenheit refer to the time meant, not to the form.
Both clauses take the Konjunktiv II. *Wenn* can be left out, and then the verb comes first.

ul: Possible now: *Wenn ich Zeit {cop:hätte}, {cop:würde} ich {cop:reisen}.*
Impossible, in the past: *Wenn ich Zeit {cpa:gehabt hätte}, {cpa:wäre} ich {cpa:gereist}.*
Without *wenn*: *{cop:Hätte} ich Zeit, {cop:würde} ich {cop:reisen}.*

konjunktiv_2_gegenwart.title: Konjunktiv II: Gegenwart
konjunktiv_2_gegenwart.summary: Would do: unreal situations, polite requests, wishes and advice.
body: Most verbs use *würde* and the infinitive.
Common verbs have their own forms, based on the Präteritum with an umlaut where possible, and the endings *-e, -est, -e, -en, -et, -en*.
Also: *dürfte, möchte, sollte, wollte, wüsste, käme, ginge, bräuchte.* *Sollen* and *wollen* have no umlaut.

ul: Unreal conditions: *Wenn ich reich {cop:wäre}, {cop:würde} ich viel {cop:reisen}.*
Polite requests: *{cop:Könnten} Sie mir {cop:helfen}? Ich {cop:hätte} gern einen Kaffee.*
Wishes: *Wenn ich doch mehr Zeit {cop:hätte}!*
Advice: *Du {cop:solltest} mehr schlafen.*

konjunktiv_2_vergangenheit.title: Konjunktiv II: Vergangenheit
konjunktiv_2_vergangenheit.summary: Would have done: what did not happen.
body: Use *hätte* or *wäre* and the Partizip II. The choice of auxiliary is the same as in the Perfekt.
With a modal verb, there are two infinitives at the end: *Ich {cpa:hätte kommen können}.*

ul: A condition and result that did not happen: *Wenn ich gelernt {cpa:hätte}, {cpa:hätte} ich {cpa:bestanden}.*
Regret or criticism: *Das {cpa:hättest} du mir {cpa:sagen sollen}.*
Wishes about the past: *{cpa:Wäre} ich doch {cpa:gekommen}!*

imperativ.title: Imperativ
imperativ.summary: Commands, requests, advice and instructions, for every way of addressing someone.

ul: *du*: take the *du* form of the present and remove *-st*. The pronoun is left out.
*ihr*: identical to the present, with no pronoun.
*Sie* and *wir*: the infinitive form, followed by the pronoun.
The vowel change *e → i* stays: *du sprichst: {imv:sprich!}; du nimmst: {imv:nimm!}; du gibst: {imv:gib!}; du liest: {imv:lies!}; du isst: {imv:iss!}*.
The umlaut *a → ä* disappears: *du fährst: {imv:fahr!}; du läufst: {imv:lauf!}*.
The final *-e* is optional and usually dropped in speech: *{imv:Komm!}* or *{imv:Komme!}*.
The *-e* is required after *-t, -d, -ig* and after some consonant groups: *{imv:Arbeite!}, {imv:Finde!}, {imv:Entschuldige!}, {imv:Öffne!}*.

body: German needs no special form. Add *nicht*, normally after the verb and any object, or use *kein* with a noun.
With an object or complement: *{imv:Mach} das nicht! {imv:Kommen Sie} nicht zu spät! {imv:Mach} keinen Lärm!*
The reflexive pronoun comes straight after the verb, and after *Sie* or *wir* in those forms. *Nicht* follows the pronoun.
The prefix goes to the end: *{imv:Steh} früh {imv:auf}! {imv:Macht} das Fenster {imv:zu}! {imv:Rufen Sie} mich {imv:an}!*

ul: Commands: *{imv:Mach} die Tür {imv:zu}!*
Requests, softened with *bitte* or *mal*: *{imv:Geben Sie} mir bitte das Salz. {imv:Komm} mal her!*
Advice: *{imv:Ruh} dich aus!*
A question is often more polite: *{cop:Könnten} Sie die Tür schließen?*
Public notices often use the infinitive: *Nicht rauchen!*

konjunktiv_1.title: Konjunktiv I
konjunktiv_1.summary: The mood of reported speech, especially in news and formal writing.
body: The Konjunktiv I signals that you are repeating what someone else said, without vouching for it. It is not used like the Italian *congiuntivo* or the Spanish *subjuntivo*.

head: Time
Example
Refers to
rows: The same time as the reported statement

body.h: When a form is the same as the indicative

body: If the Konjunktiv I looks identical to the indicative, the Konjunktiv II is used so that the reported speech is still recognisable. This happens in *ich, wir* and *sie*: *Sie sagen, sie {cop:hätten} keine Zeit.*

ul: Indirect speech in news and formal texts: *Der Minister sagte, er {csp:sei} zufrieden.*
In everyday speech people often use the indicative or *würde* instead: *Er hat gesagt, er ist zufrieden.*
Set phrases and wishes: *Es {csp:lebe} die Freiheit! Gott {csp:sei} Dank!*

konjunktiv_1_gegenwart.title: Konjunktiv I: Gegenwart
konjunktiv_1_gegenwart.summary: Reporting what someone says is true at the time.
body: Remove *-en* and add *-e, -est, -e, -en, -et, -en*. Strong verbs keep the vowel of the infinitive. *Sein* is irregular.
In practice you will mostly see the third person singular and forms of *sein*, because the others often match the indicative.

ul: *Sie sagt, sie {csp:habe} keine Zeit.*
*Der Sprecher erklärte, die Lage {csp:sei} ruhig.*
*Er behauptet, er {csp:wisse} nichts davon.*

konjunktiv_1_vergangenheit.title: Konjunktiv I: Vergangenheit
konjunktiv_1_vergangenheit.summary: Reporting what someone says happened earlier.
body: Use the Konjunktiv I of *haben* or *sein* and the Partizip II. The choice of auxiliary is the same as in the Perfekt.
It replaces all three past tenses of the original statement. Where a form matches the indicative, use *hätte* or *wäre*.

ul: *Er sagte, er {csa:habe} lange {csa:gearbeitet}.*
*Die Polizei teilte mit, der Täter {csa:sei geflohen}.*
*Sie sagen, sie {cpa:hätten} nichts {cpa:gesehen}.*

konjunktiv_1_zukunft.title: Konjunktiv I: Zukunft
konjunktiv_1_zukunft.summary: Reporting what someone says will happen.
body: Use the Konjunktiv I of *werden* and the infinitive. Where a form matches the indicative, *würde* is used instead.

ul: *Er sagte, er {fs:werde} morgen {fs:kommen}.*
*Die Regierung erklärte, sie {fs:werde} die Steuern {fs:senken}.*
*Sie sagten, sie {cop:würden} bald {cop:kommen}.*
